ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=05fab63b804f (2026-05-06T14:43:41Z) by Shenoy Pratik modified src/ad-service/src/main/resources/log4j2.xml and accidentally set the root log level to DEBUG instead of INFO for the production artifact. As a result, ad-service has been emitting extremely high-volume DEBUG logs (182,000+ lines in ~10 minutes) since that deploy reached production. The DEBUG log flood saturates the async log writer's buffer, causes blocking I/O on the log writer thread, consumes ~94% CPU, and ultimately triggers heap OOM in the log buffer allocator — cascading into gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED errors and a 67% error rate.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back ad-service to the previous known-good deploy sha=997d9970c437 to restore INFO-level logging and relieve the I/O and CPU pressure. 2. Restart the ad-service pods after rollback to clear the bloated log buffer and recover heap memory. 3. In a follow-up PR, restore log4j2.xml to use log_level=INFO for the production profile and add a CI lint/gate that rejects production build artifacts with root log level set to DEBUG. 4. Verify p99 latency and error rate return to baseline before closing the incident.
